issues.legal_issue: A sub-tenant is not entitled to purchase land under a statutory right conferred on a tenant of the landowner.
material_facts: The applicants and their fathers had occupied the land for more than thirty years as sub-tenants under a tenant who had leased it from the landowners.
The applicants applied to purchase the land under the statutory provision granting certain tenants a right to purchase land from a landowner.
The final authority and the High Court held that the applicants, as sub-tenants, were not entitled to purchase the land.
issues.conclusion: A sub-tenant is not entitled to exercise the statutory tenant’s right to purchase land from the landowner.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed section 18 alongside section 2(1) and section 2(6) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act and the definition of landowner in section 3(2) of the Punjab Land Revenue Act. The statutory purchase right applies to a tenant of a landowner; a tenant of a tenant is not thereby a tenant of the landowner. The first proviso to section 18(1), which generally bars a tenant who has sublet from applying subject to stated exceptions, does not confer the purchase right on the sub-tenant. The absence of provisions addressing competing claims, the consequences of a sub-tenant becoming owner under section 18(4)(b), and the treatment of a tenant’s rights under section 18(5) support that construction. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.application_to_purchase_land_under_tenan: The claimant applied to acquire land by invoking a statutory purchase right granted to tenants.
predicates.claimant_is_subtenant: The claimant occupied the land under a tenant rather than under the landowner.
predicates.claimant_holds_under_tenant_not_landowne: The claimant’s tenancy relationship was with an intermediate tenant, not directly with the landowner.

issues.definition: When a claimant invokes a tenant’s statutory purchase right, is a sub-tenant, and holds under an intermediate tenant rather than the landowner, the claimant is not entitled to purchase the land as a tenant.
